notes.title: Update 0.16.0: Cheer for Wrestling!
notes.notes: [p align="start"]Kept you waiting, huh?[/p][p]This update won't do the long time it took any justice. Nonetheless, it's not the smallest either and contains some pretty important things. Most importantly, however, CPW is still alive and kicking![/p][p]I could give you a long and boring story about me solo developing this as a hobby and life requiring some attention so I have less time for CPW, but you already know that.[/p][p]This update contains two things I had trouble trying to get right:[/p][olist][*][p][b]Wrestling[/b]. This is a wrestling game, duh. From lock-ups, you can now enter one of two lanes starting some back-and-forth. Finding a way to put this into CPW wasn't easy for me. The game should be as easy as possible, so this became a button mashing contest. Not very innovative, yeah, but it kind of works! Whenever you enter a wrestling situation, both wrestlers get a progress bar and whoever fills it first progresses the hold or counters it - doesn't get any easier than that! If your wrestler is already beat up or not very skilled (the Skill attribute in CAW matters), you'll have to mash harder... or maybe avoid wrestling and go for crazy stunts instead.[/p][p] [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41669788/858bba6f4d6a3e07bc073e389910fa360cc07a0e.jpg"][/img][/p][/*][*][p][b]Audible Audience Reactions[/b]. Up until now, the audience sound was but a static background noise. Now it's reactive background noise! The audience will cheer for whiplash, pop for entrances and eliminations, laugh at you when you botch a move, and boo when they get too bored (there's a setting to turn that off). There are different sounds for large and small audiences, too. The system is a work in progress, but already adds great atmosphere. Note that since there is no concept of heel or face yet - everybody's treated equally.[/p][/*][/olist][p align="start"]There are more news, such as pulling wrestlers out of the ring and there are finally a couple of moves against running opponents - check out the full changelog below.[/p][p]Before you do that, however, please know that have my utmost thanks for playing this game![/p][h3][b]Additions[/b][/h3][list][*][p][b]Actions[/b]: Added moves against opponents running towards you by pressing B (E on keyboards).[/p][list][*][p]Back Body Drop[/p][/*][*][p]Monkey Toss[/p][/*][*][p]Hurracanrana[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]Actions[/b]: Added the ability to reach into the ring from outside by pressing B (E on keyboards).[/p][list][*][p]Grabbing a wrestler by the leg will trip them up.[/p][/*][*][p]When doing a strong grab by holding the button and grabbing somebody up front, the grabbed wrestler will be pulled out of the ring.​[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]Audience[/b]: Added an audience reaction system.[/p][list][*][p]Based on their level of entertainment, the audience will be neutral, cheer or boo.[/p][/*][*][p]The audience audibly reacts to damage and other events.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]CAW[/b]: Added a new entry to the moveset editor for selecting a move against running opponents.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Menu[/b]: Added the [i]Audience Reactions[/i] setting to the Arena Setup screen with the following options:[/p][list][*][p][i]Normal[/i]: The standard audience reactions system.[/p][/*][*][p][i]No Boredom[/i]: The crowd will not get bored, even if nothing happens in the match for a long time.[/p][/*][*][p][i]None[/i]: Dead crowd.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]Wrestling[/b]: Added a wrestling system, activated by pressing [i]A[/i] ([i]SPACE[/i] on keyboards) and a direction of choice when in a lock-up.[/p][list][*][p]Wrestling is a mashing contest where participants need to fill their individual progress bars to advance to different holds or maneuvers.[/p][/*][*][p]Progress change speed is affected by a wrestler's condition as well as their [i]Skill[/i] attribute.[/p][/*][*][p]All wrestlers currently share the same wrestling holds. This may be subject to change in the future.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]Wrestling[/b]: Added wrestling holds and maneuvers.[/p][list][*][p]Headlock / Ground Headlock / Ground Headlock Pin / Headlock Suplex[/p][list][*][p]Using LB to counter the ground headlock will trigger the ground headlock pin.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Wristlock (a.k.a. Armwringer) / Hammerlock[/p][/*][/list][/*][/list][h3][b]Changes[/b][/h3][list][*][p][b]Audience[/b]: The ambient audience sound has been updated.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Menu[/b]: In the Create-A-Wrestler menu, you can now use page navigation ([i]LB[/i]/[i]RB[/i] on gamepads, [i]Page Up[/i]/[i]Page Down[/i] on keyboards) to skip 10 entries for faster navigation.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Menu[/b]: The default keyboard binding for next/previous page is now [i]Page Up[/i]/[i]Page Down[/i]. The old bindings ([i]LAlt[/i] / [i]Tab[/i]) are still working.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Physics[/b]: Increased friction coefficients for wrestler skins as well as the ring mat. This should cause somewhat less weird sliding around, especially following some moves.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Roster[/b]: Assigned moves against running opponents.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Roster[/b]: Made Private Payne stronger.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Tutorial[/b]: At the start of some of the early lessons, the opponent is now teleported right in front of you.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Tutorial[/b]: Removed quick move lesson.[/p][/*][/list][h3][b]Fixes[/b][/h3][list][*][p][b]Actions[/b]: Fixed quick grapple moves still being available from crouching.[/p][list][*][p]Quick grapple moves have been removed entirely from the codebase now.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]AI[/b]: Fixed AI ignoring ragdoll pinfall attempts in first fall matches.[/p][/*][*][p][b]CAW[/b]: Fixed known causes of data loss when filesystem operations fail when saving a CAW.[/p][/*][*][p][b]CAW[/b]: Fixed imported content being copied once per use (e.g., the same stamp on multiple attires), potentially causing too many file operations in a too short time period.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Content Packs[/b]: Fixed imported SVG files not being rendered properly.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Count-Out[/b]: Fixed multiple simultaneous count-outs not working properly, as well as the "Count Out" announcement not being played.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Netplay[/b]: Fixed run steering not being transmitted to clients.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Roster[/b]: Fixed Peggy's attributes being all default.[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Update 0.15.6: Stuff
notes.notes:
While I'm still working on getting some [b]wrestling[/b] into CPW, here's an update containing more or less random goodies!

[h3]Additions[/h3][list][*][b]Input[/b]: It is now possible to slightly change the direction while running by holding [i]Left Stick[/i] (WASD on keyboards) in the desired direction.[list][*]The direction change speed is governed by the wrestler's speed.
[*]Pressing against the current direction, as before, will cause the wrestler to stop running.[/list][previewyoutube=AQw31Rps1K0;full][/previewyoutube]
[*][b]Input[/b]: You can now slightly steer your wrestler when they are ragdolling by using holding [i]Left Stick[/i] (WASD on keyboards) in the corresponding direction. This will apply a small force to the upper body, which can be used to somewhat control the direction in which the wrestler is falling.
[previewyoutube=z8JfslyAlbk;full][/previewyoutube]
[*][b]Rules[/b]: Added a [i]Time Limit[/i] match rule.[list][*]When the match time reaches the time limit, the match is ruled a time limit draw.
[*]If a time limit is in place, the match time display will show the remaining time rather than the already passed time.
[*]Time limits are not available for matches where new participants enter after the bell (e.g., for timed battle royals).[/list][/list][h3]Changes[/h3][list][*][b]AI[/b]: If applicable, AI will now rotate moves towards a direction prioritized in the following order.[list]
[*]In battle royals, when inside the ring, moves will be rotated towards the nearest ropes as an attempt to eliminate the victim.
[*]When inside the ring, if the victim of the move is ready to be pinned, the move will be rotated towards the center.
[*]In case there is a nearby bulky weapon (e.g., stairs or tables), it will be targeted.
[*]If none of the above applies, a random direction is chosen.[/list]
[*][b]Arena[/b]: Removed the Christmas trees from the stage.
[*][b]CAW[/b]: Attires are now selected from a grid dialog featuring thumbnail previews.
[previewyoutube=51OPXpDs9iE;full][/previewyoutube]
[*][b]CAW[/b]: Split up [i]Arms & Hands[/i] and [i]Legs & Feet[/i] categories into separate categories ([i]Arms[/i], [i]Hands[/i], [i]Legs[/i], and [i]Feet[/i]).
[*][b]CAW[/b]: When adding a new attire (or editing an empty entry), the attire selection dialog is shown automatically.
[*][b]CAW[/b]: When saving a wrestler, the old CAW file is now backed up before for the case that saving fails.[list]
[*]The backup file will be contained in the wrestler's directory and have a [i].bak[/i] extension. Already existing backups will be overwritten.
[*]Restoring a backup is done by removing the [i].bak[/i] extension (the file should then have a [i].caw[/i] extension). If this is ever necessary, please contact the developer.[/list][*][b]Logging[/b]: Log entries now contain a timestamp.
[*][b]Logging[/b]: The game now keeps the 10 most recent logfiles and their filenames contain their creation timestamps.
[*][b]Menus[/b]: The pages in grid selection dialogs are now sorted alphabetically by the category.
[*][b]Moves[/b]: The Fingerpoke of Doom is no longer selected at random when randomizing a moveset. This behaviour may also apply for future moves that are more iconic than serious.[/list][h3]Fixes[/h3][list][*][b]AI[/b]: Fixed AI failing to slide into the ring from running, e.g., when entering a Timed Battle Royal.
[*][b]AI[/b]: Fixed AI sometimes "charging up" a grapple but then going for a strike anyway.
[*][b]Input[/b]: Fixed being able to springboard (and also technically slide) right after hitting the ropes. There is now a small delay like for halting.[/list]

notes.title: Anniversary and Update 0.15.4: CAW Stuff
notes.notes:
Well, would you look at that? It's CPW's first anniversary!

A year ago, after deciding there's no good reason anymore to hide CPW from the public and that its further development would benefit from a release, I finally pulled the trigger on that. Even in lack of a great fanfare (referring to my marketing budget and effort of near-zero) and considering how much things have been and still are missing for this to be a complete wrestling game experience, CPW has far exceeded my very low expectations. To give you some numbers, back then I would have been happy if the game sold a hundred times. That number was crushed before Christmas was over and as of right now, make that times ten and then some! That threw my motivation off the charts and for that, [b]thank you![/b]

Across 17 updates over the past year - some very small and some much bigger - I can safely draw the conclusion that my idea worked out and CPW's development did benefit from an early Early Access release. Core gameplay has improved plenty, and at the same time I was able to deliver (at least one part) of a major update to add more moves to the game, which is what players seemed and still seem to want most. Despite its pretty early stage still, the game has received surprisingly positive reviews here on Steam, which seems to confirm my go at things. Trust me that makes me very happy and keeps me motivated! [b]Thank you![/b]

Talking about things keeping me motivated, I had been working very hard to get the Create-A-Wrestler mode fully integrated with the Steam Workshop for the Early Access release and man, did that pay out. The workshop counts over 1,000 creations from rebuilds and caricatures of real wrestlers next to totally crazy creations. A big shout out and honorary mention goes to [i]JJ_Strife[/i] who outdid themselves by creating hundreds of those, most in jaw-dropping quality which I didn't think possible myself given the resources. Playing timed battle royals with a random selection of these CAWs is nothing short of funny and that's exactly what Casual Pro Wrestling, in its core, was supposed to be. So yet again, [b]thank you![/b]

Now I'm sitting here at the game's first anniversary - and also Christmas, by the way - and I don't have that massive update to throw out there that changes everything. Overall, I couldn't provide as much new content in this year's second half as I wanted. I have been stating and I will keep stressing that this is a one-man freetime effort. Until last year, that was next to an actual job and a little family with a baby boy. Since about halfway into this year, add to that that we're building a home for this little family, which by the way grew by one person in the meantime! Free time is a very limited resource right now and that's really the main thing holding me back from working upon the game. So please, never take the lack and sometimes small extent of updates as me "phasing out" on the game. The opposite is the case, I'm still kinda "phasing in", and, even if slowly, CPW will be developed for many years to come.

So I'll be very direct here: I've been unable to finish the update adding more wrestling-type moves such as headlocks and wristlocks and transitions between them. I hope to be able to release that in winter still, about 2-3 months into 2025, before going for the next major update. However, I am very happy to be able to provide an update that's definitely been missing in the past year. How does that meme go? It ain't much, but it's honest work!

[h2]Update 0.15.4: CAW Stuff[/h2]

Let's hit 2,000 wrestler creations in 2025! What do we need for that? Right - more content for Create-A-Wrestler! So here goes.

This update adds some Create-A-Wrestler items that have been requested. It also greatly alleviates the problem of placed stamps going completely off after editing a wrestler's body shape, especially their height.

[*][b]CAW[/b]: Added heterochromia: wrestlers can now have differing left and right eyes.

[*]Male[list]

[*]Shoes[/list][/list][*][b]Options[/b]: Added [i]Show Kickout Bar[/i] option to enable or disable display of the kickout bar, or enable it only for human-controlled wrestlers.[/list][h3]Changes[/h3][list]
[*][b]Arena[/b]: Placed Christmas trees on the stage!
[*][b]CAW[/b]: Eyes are now edited in a new submenu in the [i]Skins[/i] menu. Depending on whether Heterochromia is active or not, you will see buttons to edit each eye individually.

This greatly mitigates stamps going off when editing the body after placing them to the point where it should only be possible to notice in very irregular places (due to technical limitations and the lack of a proper definition as to what is "perfect" here, there always remains some small amount of error).

Stay tuned and to those who celebrate it: Merry Christmas!

notes.title: Update 0.15.2: Kickouts
notes.notes:
This update adds a kickout system for pinfalls, submissions and similar scenarios such as mount. It also changes grappling to be collision-based, stabilizes ragdoll-based pinfalls and fixes a bunch of bugs.

[h3]Additions[/h3][list]
[*][b]Kickout[/b]: New kickout system for pinfalls, submissions and similar.[list]
[*]You now have to actively kick out of pins and retaliate against submission holds by tapping buttons.
[*]There is a progress bar that tells you how close you are to kicking out.
[*]The maximum allowed mash rate is 8 taps per second - the closer you get to exactly that, the faster you will kick out.
[*]Pins will default to just last, so you can now also opt to let yourself be pinned. Wrestlers can no longer simply stand up from a ragdoll pinfall.
[*]Submissions may still alternatively be escaped by moving towards the ropes or end automatically if the holder's energy is exhausted.[/list][*][b]Mounting[/b]: Added the ability to kick out of a mounting situation. This uses the same kickout system as for pinfalls and submissions.[/list]
[h3]Changes[/h3][list]
[*][b]AI[/b]: Updated AI evaluation of whether or not to go for a pinfall.
[*][b]AI[/b]: Will no longer simply stand up while being on the good end of a ragdoll pinfall, but wait how it turns out.
[*][b]Grapple[/b]: Grappling is now collision-based. When you go for a grapple, your wrestler will play a grappling animation. Only if and once the hands collide with another wrestler, they will be grappled. This should completely fix cases where wrestlers temporarily freeze shortly before being grappled or turned around, and it also makes it possible to anticipate and quickly dodge a grapple attempt.
[*][b]Mounting[/b]: Sped up the animation to leave a mounting position.[/list]
[h3]Fixes[/h3][list]
[*][b]Moves[/b]: Fixed springboard Coffin Drops freezing and ultimately ragdolling a wrestler trying to execute it.
[*][b]Moves[/b]: Fixed the awkward behaviour of the Standing Sleeper Hold counter.
[*][b]Moves[/b]: Fixed the Superkick's hit detection.
[*][b]Physics[/b]: Fixed being able to perform ground moves through barricades.
[*][b]Ragdoll Pinfall[/b]: Fixed ragdoll pinfalls being stopped prematurely when involved ragdolls move slightly. They are now much more stable.
[*][b]Roll[/b]: Fixed roll attempt (block + direction while ragdolling) success evaluation being done every frame while a direction is held, unreasonably boosting the success chance. It's now down to at most one check when beginning to hold a direction, as originally intended.[/list]

notes.title: Patch 0.15.1

This patch fixes a netplay issue and applies some minor improvements to moves.

[h3]Changes[/h3][list]
[*][b]Moves[/b]: Move rotation now centers around the instigator and no longer the centroid of the involved wrestlers.
[*][b]Moves[/b]: Revised depenetration timing for Electric Chair Drop, Electric Chair Facebuster and Powerbomb Throw for improved environment interaction.[/list]
[h3]Fixes[/h3][list]

[*][b]Netplay[/b]: Fixed being unable to join a network game if the host has too many active Steam Workshop content items.[/list]

notes.title: Update 0.15.0: Moves Update #1
notes.notes:
Alright, here it is! This is the first part of CPW's first major update. It focuses on adding many new moves, individual movesets featuring a move selection in CAW mode, springboard flying attacks and a set of new entrance themes.

This sets two big milestones for CPW: First, and most importantly, not all wrestlers share the same moves anymore but they can have their individual moveset. Sure, the selection is still sparse compared to other games, but slowly we'll be getting there. [b]This is by far not the last update adding new moves![/b] Second, all stock wrestlers now have their individual entrance themes, some possibly sharing them with their future teammates.

The springboard flying attacks are a neat new gameplay feature that should really add upon the madness. Your flying attacks are now available to be performed from the top rope to the outside or from the second rope to the inside (backward).

The full changelog follows below.

notes.title: Update 0.14.20: Timing Matters!
notes.notes:
Before the first batch of new moves arrives in summer, this update addresses move countering. The way to counter moves so far was "hold LT and hope for the best". The idea behind this was to give something different from the science that other wrestling games make of countering a move. However, this turned out not too popular.

The new system focuses more on timing the press of LT properly, as it is known from many other wrestling games. To put it briefly: the better you time the button press, the more likely you are to successfully counter a move. In online games, the ping of a connected player is respected. You can learn the new system using the new Counter Feedback setting: if you activate it, whenever you try to block a move, you will get a brief message telling you whether you pressed too early, too late or whether you hit it perfectly. The setting is off by default.

You can read more about the new countering in [url=http://casualprowrestling.com/manual/gameplay/counter/]the manual[/url], which also includes some details for the nerds out there!

Here's the full changelog of update 0.14.20:

[h3]Additions[/h3][list][*][b]Options[/b]: Added the [i]Counter Feedback[/i] setting that displays a message whether the [i]Block[/i]button was pressed too early, too late, too often or (close to) perfectly when attempting a counter. It is also available in the pause menu.[/list]
[h3]Changes[/h3][list][*][b]Counters[/b]: Countering moves and grapples is now largely affected by timing the press of the [i]Block[/i] button ([i]LT[/i] on gamepads, [i]C[/i] on keyboards) correctly.[list]
[*]While a move is executed, there are one or more "sweet spots" that depend on the move at which a counter is possible (e.g., right after going into a standing head scissors for a powerbomb, or at the peak after lifting them up for the powerbomb).
[*]The shorter the time between the sweet spot and the press of the button, the higher the chance becomes to successfully counter. Mashing the button is penalized.
[*]Successful counters also depend on the momentum of the involved wrestlers.
[*]More details can be found in the [url=http://casualprowrestling.com/manual/gameplay/counter/]manual on counters[/url].
[*]The system also applies to grapples that are being initiated.
[*]In netplay, the ping of connected players is respected.
[/list]
[*][b]Tutorial[/b]: The tutorial has been updated for the new countering mechanics. During the countering lesson, the new [i]Counter Feedback[/i] setting is enforced.[/list]
[h3]Fixes[/h3][list]
[*][b]CAW[/b]: Fixed artifacts when trying to paint stamps on some hairstyles, particularly if they are mirrored.
[*][b]CAW[/b]: Fixed UV maps of female muscle shirt and tank top so painting stamps on them no longer creates artifacts.[list]
[*]When loading wrestlers with in Create-A-Wrestler mode, any existing paintjobs on these particular attires may have to be re-done.[/list]
[*][b]Flying Moves[/b]: Fixed some flying moves not working when the affected directions were held.[/list]

notes.title: Modding Update #1: Stamps & Overlays
notes.notes:
This update introduces the first modding featuring to CPW, making it possible to add custom stamps and overlay textures to Create-A-Wrestler mode. This comes with other minor improvements.

If you're interested into modding, you're kindly invited to [url=https://discord.gg/wXWh9j8Kkc]join the Discord server[/url] for asking questions, making suggestions and sharing your creations!

[h3]Modding[/h3][list]
[*][b]Content[/b]: Overlay textures (diffuse and normal maps) and stamps can now be imported from files and the Steam Workshop.[list]
[*]They can be imported directly to a created wrestler. See the manual on [url=http://casualprowrestling.com/manual/content/import/]Importing Content[/url] for more information.
[*]You can also create content packs with overlay textures and stamps and share them on the Steam Workshop for others to use! See the manual on [url=http://casualprowrestling.com/manual/content/content-packs/]Content Packs[/url] for more information and an example.[/list][/list]
[h3]Additions[/h3][list]
[*][b]Content[/b]:  The main menu will now show a message next to the [i]Content[/i] button if new content has been installed (e.g., from the Steam Workshop). In the [i]Content[/i] menu, new entries are highlighted.[list]
[*]The first time after updating the game to this version, previously deactivated content is treated as new content even if it is not actually newly installed.[/list][/list]
[h3]Changes[/h3][list]
[*][b]CAW[/b]: Overlay textures are now selected from a grid similar to stamps and organized into categories. This also allows selecting any clothing texture for hair, or any hair texture for clothing.
[*][b]CAW[/b]: Stamps are now organized into categories.
[*][b]CAW[/b]: When opening the stamp selection, the currently active stamp is now selected by default[/list]
[h3]Fixes[/h3][list]
[*][b]AI[/b]: Fixed AIs that are in a hurry running at the apron from very steep angles when already close to it, making them unable to slide in.
[/list]
[h3]Technical[/h3][list]
[*][b]AI[/b]: Updated the pathfinding backend.
[*][b]Engine[/b]: Updated Unity (to 2022.3.21).[/list]

notes.title: Update 0.14.18
notes.notes:
This update improves various gameplay aspects, particularly allowing to turn opponents to face you as well as more intuitive move rotation that allows you to aim for stuff!

Note that the binding for move rotation has changed from [i]Right Stick[/i] to [i]Left Stick[/i].

[h3]Additions[/h3][list]
[*][b]Actions[/b]: Grappling an opponent from a side will now turn them around facing you, creating the opportunity for a lock-up or grapple.
[*][b]Animation[/b]: When pressing down the [i]Grapple[/i] button, a "charging" animation is now played while holding it to give immediate feedback.[/list]
[h3]Changes[/h3][list]
[*][b]AI[/b]: Reworked the AI's way to dispatch input so that they can no longer "hold" buttons instantly but take as much time as an actual controller would.
[*][b]Animation[/b]: Updated several animations for proper transitioning from the new grapple charging animation.
[*][b]Damage[/b]: Dizziness is no longer completely reset when receiving damage while already dizzy. This should reduce the time spent on the ground while being attacked.[list]
[*]Heavy damage (e.g., from chairs or running/flying moves) will now increase the remaining dizziness time by 25% (but at most reset it).
[*]Weak damage (e.g., from stomps) will no longer affect the remaining dizziness timer at all.[/list]
[*][b]Damage[/b]: Weak damage can no longer cause a wrestler to go dizzy.
[*][b]Input[/b]: Move rotation has been changed to [i]aim[/i] into a direction.[list]
[*]When slamming or throwing an opponent or similar, they will be slammed into the held direction.
[*]For flying moves that allow rotation (e.g., the Frog Splash), the wrestler will rotate to face the held direction.[/list]
[*][b]Input[/b]: Move rotation has been rebound to the [i]left[/i] stick (WASD un keyboards).
[*][b]Input[/b]: When grappling into the nothing, control is now given back earlier during the animation.
[*][b]Irish Whip[/b]: Irish Whips are now available from lock-ups (with a 10% higher counter chance).
[*][b]Irish Whip[/b]: Irish Whips now have move rotation enabled, allowing to choose the direction at which to launch the opponent.[/list]
[h3]Fixes[/h3][list]
[*][b]AI[/b]: Fixed AI insisting on completing a navigation link (e.g., climbing ropes) even when that failed. This should fix cases of AI wrestlers ghostwalking into walls.
[*][b]Input[/b]: Fixed grapple binding from crouching to behave the same way as when standing.[/list]

notes.title: Patch 0.14.17
notes.notes:
This patch addresses miscellaneous issues.

[h3]Changes[/h3][list]
[*][b]Menus[/b]: Added a hint on the [i]Wrestler Select[/i] screen that you can hold [i]Y[/i] ([i]R[/i] on keyboards) to randomize all following selections.
[*][b]Menus[/b]: In the [i]Wrestler Select[/i] screen, holding [i]B[/i] ([i]ESC[/i] on keyboards) now unselects all wrestlers at once and goes to the previous screen.
[*][b]Moves[/b]: Disabled depenetration for several moves once letting loose: Back Drop, Body Slam, German Suplex, Powerbomb, Suplex.
[*][b]Moves[/b]: The Back Drop now has the victim's position adjusted to the instigator's height and slows down for heavier victims.[/list]
[h3]Fixes[/h3][list]
[*][b]Matches[/b]: Fixed the countdown appearing sometimes even after the last participant has entered. This caused an internal loop that would never allow the match to end.
[*][b]Menus[/b]: Fixed Attendance being unselectable when entering the [i]Arena Setup[/i] screen.
[*][b]Netplay[/b]: Fixed an error preventing that the same wrestler can be loaded up multiple times at the beginning of a match, causing connecting players to time out. This problem was specific to network games.
[*][b]Physics[/b]: Fixed wrestlers occasionally being warped back to the center of the ring in the Training Gym due to overly strict world bounds.[/list]

notes.title: Patch 0.14.16
notes.notes:
This patch addresses performance problems related to having [i]many[/i] wrestlers created and/or installed.

[h3]Changes[/h3][list]
[*][b]Performance[/b]: Fixed full-body renders of wrestlers being kept in memory at all times, potentially causing the system to run out of memory if the roster is very large. Renders are now loaded on-demand, which may cause very brief delays in the wrestler selection as a trade-off. As a side effect, this change should also lower the game's startup time.[/list]

notes.title: Update 0.14.15
notes.notes:
Thank you all for your feedback on AI Difficulty!

This update adds some customization of the AI's behaviour, allows having matches in the training gym and addresses a variety of other issues.

[h3]Additions[/h3][list]
[*][b]Menus[/b]: Added an arena selection that allows choosing from the default arena and the training gym.
[*][b]Menus[/b]: Added a [i]Custom[/i] AI mode that can be selected in the [i]Player Setup[/i] screen and allows for tweaking some AI parameters via the [i]Customize[/i] menu.[list]
[*][b]Counters[/b] – Scales the overall AI counter success chance.
[*][b]Striking / Grappling[/b] – Tweaks the fighting style of the AI.
[*][b]Decisions[/b] – Sets how fast or slow the AI takes to decide what to do next between actions.[/list][url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41669788/0dff03a22d85eb7ecf35f8fe62b6413bc660ed98.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41669788/75e4b0e970bcd30d1bcc75bd88b51e3ddcf68e6f.png[/img][/url][/list]
[h3]Changes[/h3][list]
[*][b]AI[/b]: No longer attempts to block running strikes but will instead dodge.
[*][b]AI[/b]: When outside and in a hurry (e.g., due to an impending count-out), AI will now run towards the ring even when close to it.
[*][b]Arenas[/b]: The Training Gym has undergone some changes to allow for entrances.
[*][b]Counters[/b]: To an extent, the chance of successful counters now scaled with the wrestler's Energy. This should make counters less common towards the end of the match.
[*][b]Dodge[/b]: The dodge animation speed now depends on the wrestler's Speed attribute and current condition.
[*][b]Grapple[/b]: Sanitized grapple and lock-up positioning.
[*][b]Moves[/b]: Disabled depenetration for Suplex once the victim is lifted.
[*][b]Menus[/b]: When going back from the ready screen, only the last wrestler is unselected now and no longer all.
[*][b]Netplay[/b]: The match join timeout time has been increased and scales with the number of wrestlers to be loaded.
[*][b]Reactions[/b]: Heavy strikes now interrupt lock-ups, grapples and ongoing moves.
[*][b]Settings[/b]: Settings are now saved in the file [i]Preferences.json[/i] in the game's data directory and no longer in the Windows registry.
[*][b]Settings[/b]: The [i]Entrances[/i] setting from the arena setup is now memorized between game sessions.[/list]
[h3]Fixes[/h3][list]
[*][b]CAW[/b]: Fixed negative weights being possible by setting an absolute minimum weight of 30 kg (~66 lbs).
[*][b]Input[/b]: Fixed grappling, striking and running input being accepted prematurely while standing up, causing unintendedly rough transitions.
[*][b]Match Setup[/b]: Fixed the result of matches declared unsanctioned being counted anyway.
[*][b]Menus[/b]: Fixed back button in the ready screen being unclickable if there are many wrestler renders showing.
[*][b]Menus[/b]: Fixed ring names not being localized.
[*][b]Netplay[/b]: Ensure that connecting players receive a remote controller after joining. This should fix cases where joining players cannot control anything.[/list]

notes.title: Patch 0.14.14
notes.notes:
This patch fixes ground move warping and a few other things.

[h3]Changes[/h3][list]
[*][b]Reactions[/b]: Introduced a minimum velocity in addition to minimum impulse for a ragdoll to cause a strike when hitting another wrestler. This should mitigate issues handling really heavy wrestlers when they are grounded.[/list]
[h3]Fixes[/h3][list]
[*][b]AI[/b]: Fixed AI potentially getting stranded on the apron when in a navigation behaviour (e.g., eliminated wrestlers leaving the arena).
[*][b]AI[/b]: Fixed AI sometimes still getting stuck in a loop attempting to drag an opponent.
[*][b]Physics[/b]: Fixed scheduled collision enabling overriding any disabling that occurred meanwhile (and vice versa). This was the root cause for a lot of unwanted warping and displacement affecting mostly ground moves (due to the timing), including the infamous Camel Clutch warp.
[*][b]Menus[/b]: Fixed match result screen showing after making changes in the [i]Content[/i] screen when a match has been finished earlier in the same game session.[/list]

notes.title: Patch 0.14.13
notes.notes:
This patch contains some critical fixes.

[h3]Fixes[/h3][list]
[*][b]Netplay[/b]: Fixed online matches being invisible.
[*][b]Steam Workshop[/b]: Fixed only the first 50 shared Workshop items having their share information correctly displayed.[/list]

notes.title: Patch 0.14.12
notes.notes:
This patch contains some AI hotfixes.

[h3]Changes[/h3][list]
[*][b]AI[/b]: Made the AI slightly more pessimistic about pinfalls. This should cause them to stop dragging around rather healthy opponents.
[*][b]AI[/b]: Adjusted the AI's way of determining whether an opponent is near the ropes and should be dragged towards the center of the ring.[/list]
[h3]Fixes[/h3][list]
[*][b]AI[/b]: Fixed the AI still freezing at times trying to drag their opponents to the center of the ring.[/list]

notes.title: Patch 0.14.11
notes.notes:
This patch tweaks the camera, adds a camera angle setting to the pause menu, adjusts pinfalls, reduces the Energy loss when receiving damage, adds QOL features to the Content screen and fixes bugs.

[h3]Additions[/h3][list]
[*][b]Content Screen[/b]: Added a button to activate or deactivate all content.
[*][b]Settings[/b]: Added the [i]Camera Angle[/i] setting to the pause menu.[/list]
[h3]Changes[/h3][list]
[*][b]Arena[/b]: Removed the Christmas trees from the stage.
[*][b]Camera[/b]: Various improvements regarding the camera.[list]
[*]It is now allowed to fly along the foward axis to better follow the action.
[*]Its flight speed has been increased.
[*]The FOV computation has been reworked from the ground up.[/list]
[*][b]CAW[/b]: Adjusted the lower limit for the Feet Length morph so feet won't go inside themselves anymore.
[*][b]Content Screen[/b]: Navigating left from any list entry will now immediately jump to the [i]Apply[/i] button.
[*][b]Pinfall[/b]: Tweaked the influence of Stats on pinfall outcome and reduced random adjustment.[list]
[*]Pinfalls are no longer be possible at full health.[/list]
[*][b]Stats[/b]: Lowered the maximum amount of Energy loss when receiving damage.[/list]
[h3]Fixes[/h3][list]
[*][b]AI[/b]: Fixed some details about AI handling links (e.g., apron, barricades) and implemented a watchdog that will get an AI out of walking straight into one direction should traversal fail somehow.
[*][b]AI[/b]: Fixed AI freezing when deciding to drag the opponent to the ring center while outside the ring.
[*][b]Collision[/b]: Fixed sorrounding collisions causing wrestlers to be placed apart for Boston Crab, Camel Clutch and mounting.[/list]

notes.title: Patch 0.14.10
notes.notes:
This patch adds apron side punches, fixes a number of bugs and improves plenty of situations where wrestlers are inexplicably immune to strikes and grapples.

[h3]Additions[/h3][list]
[*][b]Apron[/b]: Added punches to the side. These are used when striking at targets that are also the same apron next to a wrestler.
[*][b]CAW[/b]: Added value displays next to sliders.[/list]
[h3]Changes[/h3][list]
[*][b]AI[/b]: After a low randomized number of ground attacks, the AI will stop going for more for a few seconds. This should mitigate stomp loops.
[*][b]Apron[/b]: After receiving a certain amount of damage, similar to sitting or in a corner, wrestlers will now ragdoll from the apron.
[*][b]CAW[/b]: Rearranged the attributes so they are in the same order as they are shown in the wrestler selection.
[*][b]Counter[/b]: Changed how wrestler stats influence a wrestler's counter score: Energy and Momentum now the same influence, the influence of Health has been lowered somewhat.
[*][b]Counter[/b]: Decreased the maximum chance of a successful counter.
[*][b]Counter[/b]: Skill now influences the counter scores.[list]
[*]It is easier to counter moves of less skilled wrestlers and vice versa.[/list]
[*][b]Grapple[/b]: Performing a weak strike no longer grants grapple immunity at all.
[*][b]Input[/b]: Changed lock-up and grapple triggers to how they were before beta 0.11.0:[list]
[*]Entering a lock-up is now done by [i]tapping[/i] A (E on keyboards).
[*]Entering a grapple is now done by [i]holding[/i] A (E on keyboards).
[*]Quick grapple moves have been moved to [i]holding[/i] B (R on keyboards), though this may not be permanent.[/list]
[*][b]Pace[/b]: Increased wrestler base acceleration by 33%.
[*][b]Pace[/b]: Sped up the front and back grapple entering animations by 25%.
[*][b]Pace[/b]: Sped up the stair stepping animations by 25%.
[*][b]Reactions[/b]: Reduced or removed strike and grapple immunity in several situations where it used to span the entire animation.[list]
[*]Climbing in or out of the ring.
[*]Climbing up or down an apron.
[*]Climbing the top turnbuckle.
[*]Climbing onto the stage.
[*]Jumping onto a barricade.
[*]Picking up, placing or throwing a weapon.[/list]
[*][b]Reactions[/b]: Removed complete strike immunity for a half second following climbing an apron.
[*][b]Stats[/b]: A fraction of incoming damage determined by a wrestler's Health is now also applied to their Energy.[/list]
[h3]Fixes[/h3][list]
[*][b]AI[/b]: Fixed AI prematurely aborting any attempt to drag their victim towards the center of the ring prior to going for a pinfall, and sometimes not even considering it.
[*][b]AI[/b]: Fixed AI not attacking wrestlers on a barricade or jump-ready on the stage.
[*][b]Corner[/b]: Fix corner occupation not cleared when prematurely exiting a climb animation (e.g., due to ragdolling), causing the corner to become unclimbable by others.
[*][b]Corner[/b]: Implemented a regular check to make sure that wrestlers who are believed to occupy a corner are actually there. This should fix corners becoming impossible to climb if anything goes wrong.
[*][b]Count-Out[/b]: Fixed eliminated wrestlers potentially still being counted out.
[*][b]Elimination[/b]: Fixed non-ragdolling wrestlers being eliminated prematurely in some situations.
[*][b]Flying Moves[/b]: When performing a flying move while holding a weapon, that weapon is now ignored for mid-air collision detection, which caused the wrestler to instantly ragdoll for some moves.
[*][b]Reactions[/b]: Fixed wrestlers being immune to strikes when sitting on a barricade or jump-ready on the stage.
[*][b]Rules[/b]: Fixed the match continuing after everyone has been eliminated and the last participant enters after.[/list]

notes.title: Patch 0.14.9
notes.notes:
This patch mainly fixes the AI ceiling stare bug, some AI stupidity regarding weapons and applies some conservative pace changes.

[h3]Changes[/h3][list]
[*][b]AI[/b]: When trying to enter the ring with a larger weapon, if the target is ragdolling or far enough away, AI will now place the weapon inside the ring and go for it once inside the ring.
[*][b]AI[/b]: Will no longer leave or enter the ring just to get a weapon that they cannot traverse the apron with.
[*][b]CAW[/b]: Removed the obsolete Up/Down morph that could make wrestlers float or sink in the ground.[list]
[*]Created wrestlers have to be loaded and saved again in order to ground them.[/list]
[*][b]Grapple[/b]: Increased the distance from which grappling is possible (from 85% to 93.5% of the combined reach).
[*][b]Grapple[/b]: Increased the field of view angle from which grappling is possible (from 105° to 120°).
[*][b]Pace[/b]: Increased the base turn speed of wrestlers (from 180°/s to 225°/s).
[*][b]Pace[/b]: Made state transition movement and rotation faster overall.
[*][b]Tutorial[/b]: Additional coaches are now "hard-spawned" for targeting lessons. This may cause a brief lag spike, but that's better than having to wait for a few seconds.
[*][b]Tutorial[/b]: When coaches are despawned, it is now ensure that the player has a target afterwards.[/list]
[h3]Fixes[/h3][list]
[*][b]AI[/b]: Fixed AI ending up targeting themselves in some scenarios, causing them to stand idle and look at the ceiling.[/list]

notes.title: Patch 0.14.8
notes.notes:
This version addresses a first few bugs.

[h3]Changes[/h3]
[list]
[*][b]Steam[/b]: Disabled Steam Input by default. Unless absolutely needed for some reason, it is recommended to leave Steam Input disabled for now until issues caused by it have been addressed.
[/list]
[h3]Fixes[/h3]
[list]
[*][b]CAW[/b]: Fixed gamepads going lost when entering the [i]Entrances[/i] menu.
[*][b]Menus[/b]: Fixed the [i]Invite ...[/i] showing even if no Steam match is being hosted.
[*][b]Taunts[/b]: Fixed glitches caused by trying to use the D-Pad Right taunt (which was a leftover debugging function). It is the same as D-Pad Left for now.
[/list]

notes.title: Early Access Release Date
notes.notes:
[i]I'm afraid I've got some bad news[/i] today that may be disappointing to some, but I want to remain transparent about the game's development. I feel an announcement like this is the best way to share these news and now, as the project's popularity is still rather small, is the best time to do it.

To get straight to the point: I decided to postpone the Early Access release of Casual Pro Wrestling by one year to [b]December 22, 2023[/b]. Here's why.

Frankly, I overestimated how far the game already was when I announced it 8 months back, and how far I was gonna get it according to my internal roadmap. To some degree, I also chose a rather short time frame to boost my motivation - which, by the way, worked. CPW has already been in development for several years and I thought that by the end of this year, I could release [i]something[/i] for  Early Access. While that statement still holds, and albeit I'm a solo developer and the game literally has "Casual" in its title, I don't want to release unfinished garbage. This past month, I realized that I couldn't get the game to a state that I'd be going to be content with just until the end of the year. After some struggling about how far to postpone, I decided that a full year should give me all the room I need, also to avoid having to postpone again in the future. So there's that: I consider the new date a deadline.

I promised to be transparent, so what is it that takes so much time? The following are the bigger bullets on my roadmap for an Early Access release:
[list]
[*] Improve match flow by adding counters to moves, grappling scenarios with transitions, the ability to interact with wrestlers in "passive" states (e.g., while getting up, while perfoming a move, etc).
[*] Implement holds, effectively adding submissions to the game, in an interesting manner.
[*] Carefully balance how a wrestlers' stats affect their actions and (AI) behaviour, and how actions affect the wrestlers in the match.
[*] Add CAW content, most importantly by finishing the female model and providing basic attires for it.
[*] Create a first version of a modding kit that will allow importing rigged humanoid 3D models and make them playable wrestlers, as well as adding custom CAW content.
[*] Steam Workshop integration of CAWs, both in-game as well as 3D model imports, including making them playable in network multiplayer.
[*] Implement a first rudimentary, arcade-ish career mode for a start.
[/list]
While the list doesn't seem very long, bear in mind that every bullet requires research, creative thought processes, content creation (especially animations), programming and, to an extent, documentation, aside from the many details that come and unfold on the fly that I can't possibly list. Take into account that this is a solo hobby project with no team or noteworthy budget behind it. The named points are also core mechanics that, in my view, need to be worked out before releasing the game, even to Early Access, because a release would most certainly shift priorities and delay those things even more.

In the past months, I have posted some development blogs on selected topics and I will continue to do so. The Twitter feed, [url=https://twitter.com/CasProWrestling]@CasProWrestling[/url], is updated more regularly with mostly short gameplay clips, and you can expect that to go on as well.

I hope that the disappointment is bearable for those who have been following - sorry for that. On the bright side, a real alternative to the 2K games is coming soon and from a studio with an actual budget. I'm sure it will breathe long-awaited fresh air into the genre and inspire this project as well as the many other indie wrestling games currently in development (check out Twitter, you'd be surprised). Certainly, it will bridge the gap until everyone gets what they really want - Casual Pro Wrestling! ːsteammockingː

Feel free to ask or discuss anything about the development process and stay tuned!
